html:
The siege of Constantinople in July 1203 was the first attack on the city by the army of the Fourth Crusade and the fleet of Venice. It put the Byzantine prince Alexios Angelos on the throne and set up the sack of 1204.

The crusade had set out for Egypt but owed Venice a large debt for its ships. Alexios, son of the deposed emperor Isaac II, promised money, troops and the union of the churches if the crusaders made him emperor. They reached Constantinople in June 1203. The Venetians broke the chain across the Golden Horn and stormed part of the sea walls, with the blind doge Enrico Dandolo in front, while the knights attacked near the Blachernae Palace.

Emperor Alexios III fled the city with treasure. The Byzantines brought blind Isaac out of prison and put him back on the throne, and his son was crowned beside him as Alexios IV. But he could not pay what he had promised, and both sides came to hate him. Early in 1204 he was overthrown and killed, and the crusaders decided to take the city for themselves.
